newsitem.title: INDIA: India says Pakistani troops kill two Indian Kashmiris.
newsitem.headline: India says Pakistani troops kill two Indian Kashmiris.

text.p: Two people including a child were killed and eight injured when Pakistani troops opened fire across the border in the Indian state of Jammu and Kashmir, a Indian defence spokesman said on Saturday.
He said an old man and the child were killed in the town of Kargil in the mountainous Ladakh region on Friday evening when Pakistani troops fired on the Indian side.
Kargil is 220 km (150 miles) southwest of Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir.
"Heavy firing and mortar shelling since Wednesday forced 4,000 people of this mountainous town to abandon their homes," the spokesman said.
Earlier this week, Indian defence officials had said many families were forced to abandon their homes in Kashmir state due to heavy mortar shelling on the Indian side by Pakistani troops.
But Pakistani defence officials said nothing unusual had happened and that exchanges of fire between Indian and Pakistani troops were a routine matter.
India and Pakistan have fought two of their three wars since independence from Britain in 1947 over the disputed Himalayan region of Kashmir, of which India controls two-thirds and Pakistan the rest.
Indian and Pakistani troops frequently exchange fire across the Line of Control and the "working" border.
The "working" border between India and Pakistan stretches 174 km (109 miles) between the Chenab and Ravi rivers to join up in the north with the Line of Control, or ceasefire line, dividing Kashmir.
